established_findings: Unconditional two-step search does not improve the primary metric after RNG isolation and costs roughly 9x compute.
Historical breadth benefits are not transferable without exact executable lineage; benchmark v2 n=48 does not support unconditional width-2 superiority.

Simple breadth thresholds, local-margin depth gates, model-disagreement bonuses, proposal diversification, edge-centric utility replacement, posterior-state gating, calibration correction, variance-reduced EIG racing, and robust maximin EIG across prior classes were falsified prospectively.
Fresh benchmark v2 has frozen executable mechanics, exact 29,281-DAG support, budget 15, strict RNG isolation, and source-addressed lineage.
Fixed graph sparsity priors, strong coefficient shrinkage, g-priors, scale integration, and predictive family scoring do not provide reliable improvement.
S7 localized the promising nonlocal prior's harms to policy feedback rather than terminal inference.
S8 prospectively confirmed dual-posterior separation and S9 confirmed transfer under weaker effect sizes without retuning.

Under nonlinear mechanism shift, the frozen dual-posterior science model retains large structural-recovery gains, but ungated full-posterior calibration is unstable; disagreement-aware abstention resolves much of this failure mode.
S15 supported disagreement-aware abstention under nonlinear shift with 93.75% coverage and mean promoted edge improvement 0.587 while meeting its calibration guardrail.

Original S16 is nonpoolable because same exposed seeds produced conflicting results without a common persisted noise kernel; executable RNG consumption semantics are therefore part of the frozen experimental mechanism, not an implementation detail.

Fresh source-addressed S16R supports transfer of the fixed S15 D<=1.50 gate under standardized Student-t(df=3) noise: 87.5% confirmation coverage, mean promoted edge improvement 0.439, bootstrap 95% improvement interval [0.282,0.591], mean Brier delta +0.00141, and zero promoted large harms.

S17 falsified the one-dimensional D<=1.50 gate under compound nonlinear plus heavy-tail shift: structural recovery remained strong (mean promoted edge improvement 0.358; bootstrap 95% improvement interval [0.207,0.503]; zero large harms), but mean promoted Brier worsened by +0.00885 and breached the frozen +0.005 calibration guardrail.

S18 showed that adding worst-edge disagreement and entropy-ratio signals did not resolve the compound-shift calibration failure: fresh validation retained mean edge improvement 0.495 with 22/24 wins and zero large harms, but Brier delta +0.00628 still failed the +0.005 guardrail.
Posterior-disagreement geometry alone is now deprioritized; S19 tests whether observable posterior-predictive residual mismatch can identify the remaining model-shift-sensitive cases.
Execution reproducibility and namespace isolation remain hard scientific invariants; blocked historical worlds are never pooled.

dynamic_enqueue_rules: Every completed experiment must generate at least one next candidate unless a stronger queued candidate already tests the same uncertainty.
Falsification never empties the queue; it narrows or redirects it.
Do not enqueue equivalent retries without a changed causal hypothesis, state representation, reward, search depth, world model, or evaluation design.
Promote surprising anomalies and control victories into diagnostic experiments.
Maintain matched resource budgets and preserve all negative results.
